messages:
Maria: quick follow-up on the annotated-allocation contract RFC — want to lock down the backfill semantics before I write the formal doc. TL;DR: propose per-allocation annotation fields {prefer_resident, soft_eviction_score, backfill_policy} exposed in allocator->offloader handshake. concrete questions: sync vs async backfill? how to patch annotations for live allocations? eviction ordering across mixed annotations?

Jay: i vote async backfill with per-tenant rate limits. sync backfill will stall the hot path and make tail latency awful. :thumbsup:

Siva: async is fine but we need clear liveness guarantees and a fast fallback when backfill fails. propose default fallback: immediate re-materialize from host copy (if present) and increment attempt_count in annotation so we stop spamming offloader.

Nora: cost-wise do we even keep host copies for everything? storage & memory pressure are real. we should make host-copy policy size-tiered.

Maria: agreed. suggestion: keep host copy for small allocations (<64KB) by default, for larger ones keep checksum + recompute-hint. sketch:

```c
struct alloc_annotation {
  uint8_t prefer_resident;      // 0/1 hint
  uint8_t backfill_policy;      // 0=never,1=lazy,2=aggressive
  uint8_t retry_limit;         // number of backfill retries before fallback
  uint16_t soft_score;         // 0..65535, higher => prefer residency
};
```

Jay: another fragmentation angle — annotated small allocations will increase mixed-slab churn. we should consider allocation-class bucketing: group similar annotations into dedicated slabs so compaction/fallback is cheaper.

Siva: +1. bumping prefer_resident=1 into a dedicated slab reduces interleaving churn. downside: potential internal waste for underutilized slabs. maybe make slab-grouping adaptive: promote/demote buckets based on occupancy and soft_score heatmaps.

Maria: sounds good. also need to think about cross-tenant fairness: if one tenant annotates everything as aggressive, we shouldn't let them starve others. admission controller should consider annotation soft_score and tenant priority.

Nora: telemetry items: per-annotation miss rate, backfill queue latency, fallback frequency, slab promotion/demotion counts. add counters for re-materialize path and for recompute-hint successes.

Jay: how should Dedicated (reserved GPU) pools interact? i think tenant policy override must be allowed: Dedicated can pin regardless of prefer_resident, but should still expose metrics so infra teams can see cost delta.

alloc-bot: deploy: branch alloc/annot-bridge -> staging at 2026-03-18T09:12Z (CI passed)

Siva: operational test idea: synthetic workload that creates many small annotated tensors with alternating prefer_resident flags, then force offload pressure and measure tail latency + compaction churn. need a liveness test that simulates offloader being temporarily unreachable.

Maria: implementation plan (proposal):
1) extend allocator API with an opaque annotation blob and a tiny schema (fields above)
2) allocator groups allocations into annotation_buckets and optionally allocate from dedicated slab classes
3) offloader advertises available capacity and accepts backfill requests over async queue; queue entries carry annotation and a correlation id
4) admission controller uses soft_score + tenant policy to compute eviction priority
5) fallback path: if backfill fails or exceeds retry_limit, immediately re-materialize from host copy or run recompute-hint; record telemetry

Jay: for API ergonomics, expose helper primitives in our C++ SDK: allocate_with_annotation(sz, Annotation{...}), patch_annotation(ptr, AnnotationPatch{...}). keep the opaque blob small to avoid syscall bloat.

Nora: add to doc: recommended defaults for common workloads (chat embeddings, decoder kv caches, batch inputs). those defaults will guide product teams and avoid everyone setting aggressive flags by mistake.

Siva: one more thought — for some tensors we can avoid host-copy entirely by storing a compact digest + deterministic recompute recipe (example: ephemeral embeddings computed from fixed model inputs). that reduces host memory but requires coordination with model infra. add as opt-in recompute_hint field.

Maria: perfect. i'll draft the full design with diagrams (bucket lifecycle, backfill queue flow, and fallback states). action items: Maria write design doc by EOD Friday; Jay prototype slab-bucket mapping; Siva add liveness test; Nora add telemetry schema. i'll file follow-up PRs and link here. :rocket:

Jay: +1, thanks.

Nora: thanks — ping @eng-sre for perf/regression signoff once prototype lands.

Maria: closing loop — tagging product briefly for prioritization input. thanks everyone.
